title: Do the Burdens to Being Public Affect the Investment and Innovation of Newly Public Firms?
near_miss_reason: Main design (Equation (1), Tables 3-8) is a cross-cohort comparison: quarterly investment of newly public firms on JOBS IPO (IPO after 8 Dec 2011, fixed per firm) x Non-SRC with IPO-quarter, fiscal-quarter, calendar-quarter, IPO-year and industry FE but no firm FE, plus time-varying controls. The only within-firm design (Table 9 Panel A: JOBS IPO x Proceeds>=75 x Post-IPO, firm and year-quarter FE, IPO dates staggered) adds years-since-IPO FE (event-time main effects), the lower-order Post-IPO interactions and an industry market-to-book control, so it violates more than the controls rule.
eligible_reason: No qualifying column. Equation (1) lacks firm FE and the treatment indicator is a fixed firm attribute (IPO timing) interacted with float status; Table 9 Panel A within-firm DDD includes years-since-IPO FE and a time-varying control. Data are licensed (SDC, Compustat, CRSP) and not shipped.
design_notes: DG (2019) Stata Code.do: reghdfe invest2 c.postjobs##c.nonsrc lat ocfq mtb ln_proceeds if egc==1, absorb(q_ipo fqtr datacqtr_num year ind_code) vce(cluster gvkey datacqtr_num) (Table 3 cols 1-3; Table 4 capx/R&D). Sample: first eight full quarters after IPO for issuers with revenue < $1bn.
data_files_note: Read Me: dgsample lists SDC IPO deal numbers; hcfloat is hand-collected public float; the SAS code builds variables from licensed SDC, Compustat quarterly/annual and CRSP files that are not included.
data_provenance_note: Only identifiers and hand-collected float shipped; outcome data licensed.
